To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rabbit hepatic perfusate supernatant contains a factor VIII stimulating activity that appears in the void volume of gel‐chromatography columns and that this activity is associated with a factor VIII‐neutralization antigen.

1) factor‐VIII‐stimulating material from perfused rabbit liver is a high molecular weight protein; 2) the factor‐VIII antigen is a high molecular protein; and 3) the factor‐ VIII stimulating material contains a factor‐VIII neutralizing antigen that is a high molecular-weight protein.
the hepatic factor VIII‐stimulation system is a high‐molecular weight protein that is not identical to rabbit plasma factor VIII.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and isolation of the factor VIII‐stimulator of rabbit liver and the demonstration of a factor VIII‐neutralizer present in the hepatic effluent.
the isolation and characterization of a factor VIII stimulator in rabbit liver.
the isolation and partial characterization of the factor VIII‐stimulation factor of rabbit liver perfusates and with the relationship of this material to rabbit plasma factor VIII.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the material in rabbit hepatic perfusate that stimulates factor VIII activity is antigenically and molecularly related to rabbit factor VIII, but that it is not factor VIII itself.
the factor VIII‐stimulation activity in the perfusates is not due to the factor VIII itself but to a high‐molecular weight material which may be a precursor of factor VIII.
the factor‐VIII‐stimulating activity in hepatic perfusion fluids is a large, heterogeneous molecule that is antigenically related to rabbit factor VIII.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatic factor VIII‐stimulator is a high‐molecular weight material that is antigenically related to the factor VIII of rabbit plasma.
factor VIII is produced by the liver, is released into the circulation, and is then cleared from the blood by the spleen.
